name: Team OKR Review & Next-Quarter Plan
description: An executive quarterly OKR review in charcoal, forest green, and warm white: transparent attainment scoring, target-versus-actual evidence, outcome-led achievements, candid root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and measurable next-quarter commitments with cross-team dependencies.
style_guide:
# Team OKR Review & Next-Quarter Plan

## Purpose and narrative

Build an executive team review that closes one quarter and turns its evidence into a credible next-quarter plan. The deck must answer six management questions in sequence: What did we commit to? What did we achieve? Which operating metrics moved? What value was created? Where did we miss and why? What will the team and its partners commit to next?

The tone is analytical, composed, and accountable. It should acknowledge both achievement and underperformance without becoming defensive or celebratory. This is an OKR operating review—not a generic KPI dashboard, annual business review, project status report, product roadmap, or team-culture retrospective. Each body page should lead with a management conclusion and support it with auditable evidence.

The preview images define only the visual family and composition examples. Never copy their organization, team, objective, key result, product, metric, value, target, account, revenue, date, cause, action, or forecast. Those facts are fictional UI content. This written guide is the complete authoring authority.

## Visual identity

- Use one near-black cover followed by predominantly light, warm-gray body pages.
- Make Forest green the core identity color: titles, major panels, rules, objective labels, and strong values.
- Use brighter Emerald for confirmed success, alignment, or favorable movement. Structural green alone must not imply good performance.
- Reserve Red for an actual miss, breached threshold, or demonstrated root cause. Reserve Orange for partial attainment, watch status, or improvement that remains below target.
- Use large, sentence-style headlines that state the conclusion rather than labels such as `Metrics` or `Results`.
- Build slides from flat rectangular fields, thin borders, top rails, disciplined columns, and substantial whitespace.
- Use one editorial serif statement only when the page needs a memorable strategic thesis; keep all ordinary evidence in sans-serif type.
- Do not add photographs, illustrations, dashboards, or decorative icons. The evidence and hierarchy are the visual content.

## Canvas and layout geometry

- Author on a fixed `1280 × 720 px` 16:9 canvas.
- Keep `66–72 px` left and right margins. Keep `36–48 px` top clearance and at least `34 px` below content before the footer.
- Use a 12-column grid with `18–22 px` gutters. All title edges, cards, rules, values, status labels, and footer elements should resolve to this grid.
- Reserve `92–126 px` at the top of a body page for the eyebrow and conclusion headline. A two-line headline is acceptable; a third line means the statement should be edited.
- Keep `20–26 px` between major panels and `14–20 px` internal padding.
- Body content may use three equal columns, a `3/9` thesis-and-evidence split, or a balanced `6/6` analysis-and-action split. Do not mix several grid systems on one page.
- Use square corners or a maximum `2–3 px` radius. Use one-pixel borders and no shadows.
- Keep at least 80 percent of ordinary body-page area Warm canvas or White. Dark green is reserved for one strong rail or thesis panel.

## Color specification

### Foundation

- Cover charcoal: `#101514`. Full-cover background only, plus an optional final divider or closing statement.
- Warm canvas: `#F3F6F4`. Dominant body-page background.
- White: `#FFFFFF`. Objective cards, metric panels, achievement cards, analysis panels, and dependency fields.
- Primary ink: `#102B26`. Ordinary text, key-result descriptions, values, actions, and owners.
- Quiet gray: `#6F7875`. Comparators, explanations, footer text, metadata, and secondary notes.
- Structural gray: `#DCE3DF`. Card borders, divider lines, baselines, and footer rules.

### Green hierarchy

- Forest green: `#00583D`. Main title color, overall-review panel, strategic thesis field, objective names, strong rules, and structural emphasis.
- Achievement emerald: `#00966D`. Achieved status, favorable deltas that meet their threshold, numbered achievements, confirmed alignment, and the cover rail.
- Soft mint: `#E5F2ED`. Background for achieved labels, favorable callouts, confirmed dependencies, and executive perspective boxes.

### Exception colors

- Miss red: `#E43C42`. Missed key results, quantified gaps, breached thresholds, and the left rail of a root-cause page.
- Pale red: `#FBE9EA`. Small missed or exception labels only.
- Watch orange: `#D97A00`. Partial attainment, constrained metrics, or a result improving in the desired direction but still below target.
- Pale orange: `#FFF1D8`. Small watch or partial labels only.

### Color rules

- Never use Green, Red, or Orange decoratively. A color must correspond to a stated scoring or status rule.
- Pair color with explicit words such as `ACHIEVED`, `PARTIAL`, `MISSED`, `ALIGNED`, or an accurate localized equivalent.
- A positive delta is not automatically achievement; if the target remains missed, use Orange or Red according to the published threshold.
- Do not use gradients, translucent glass, glow, colored shadows, or multicolor chart palettes.

## Typography

- Primary family: `Inter`, `Aptos`, `Arial`, `Helvetica Neue`, or a comparable neutral sans-serif.
- Optional thesis serif: `Georgia` or `Source Serif 4`; use only for one quotation-like statement on an achievement page.
- Optional metadata mono: `IBM Plex Mono`, `Consolas`, or `Courier New`; restrict it to formulas, data locks, sources, and version labels.
- Cover title: `50–62 px`, weight `500–650`, line-height `1.05–1.12`, White.
- Cover subtitle: `22–28 px`, weight `350–450`, Quiet gray or a warm light gray.
- Body conclusion headline: `30–40 px`, weight `550–700`, line-height `1.08–1.18`, Forest green.
- Section eyebrow: `10–13 px`, weight `650–750`, uppercase, letter-spacing `1.3–2 px`, Achievement emerald.
- Hero score: `48–64 px`, weight `750–850`, tabular numerals, White when placed on Forest green.
- Objective, metric, or panel title: `18–24 px`, weight `650–750`.
- Key-result or action title: `15–19 px`, weight `600–700`.
- Body copy: `11–15 px`, weight `400–500`, line-height `1.4–1.55`.
- Status, footer, source, formula, and data note: `8–11 px`, never smaller merely to make content fit.
- For CJK output, use a common CJK sans-serif with clear medium and bold weights. Edit line breaks semantically and avoid applying Latin letter-spacing to long CJK text.

## Repeating body-page frame

- Begin with a small Emerald eyebrow naming the quarter and analytical section.
- Follow with a left-aligned, conclusion-led Forest-green headline. It should state the result, tension, or next-quarter choice in plain language.
- Align the top of all evidence panels beneath the headline. Avoid isolated floating labels.
- Use a thin Structural-gray footer rule. Put the report name at lower-left and `N/N` at lower-right.
- Place metric definitions, sources, score formulas, and data-lock dates close to the evidence they qualify. Never hide them as unreadable footnotes.

## Page 1 — Cover

- Fill the slide with Cover charcoal and place a slim vertical Achievement-emerald rail about `70–88 px` from the left edge.
- Align all text to a second vertical line roughly `65–75 px` to the right of the rail.
- Place a compact review-series or organization label in Emerald above the title.
- Use a large two-line White title naming the OKR review and the next planning period.
- Add one restrained subtitle connecting the completed period's performance to the upcoming period's strategic plan.
- Use a short horizontal Gray rule above one metadata line for presenter, role, audience, and review date.
- Preserve the broad empty charcoal field. Do not add KPI cards, charts, logos, photography, patterns, or decorative geometry.

## Page 2 — Overall attainment and objective review

- Lead with a headline that gives the overall attainment and the contrast between the strongest and weakest objective.
- Use a narrow Forest-green summary rail occupying roughly one-fifth of the content width. Show the period, overall score, score label, and a short synthesis.
- Use two equal White objective cards in the remaining space. Each card contains the objective name, objective score, a thin Emerald rule, and two to four KR records.
- Each KR record must show the KR statement, target, actual, status, and a brief evidence-based explanation. Keep status labels compact and right-aligned where possible.
- The overall score must disclose its formula, objective weights, KR weights, caps, inverse-metric treatment, stretch-goal treatment, and missing-data rule.
- `ACHIEVED`, `PARTIAL`, and `MISSED` require pre-agreed thresholds. Do not infer them from color or use a universal OKR convention without confirmation.
- Limit the main page to two or three objectives. Move full scorecard detail to an appendix.

## Page 3 — Before-and-after metric comparison

- Use three equal White columns on the Warm canvas. Each column represents one business or operating metric.
- At the top of each column show a metric number and category, metric name, and one-line definition.
- Separate context from the numeric comparison with a thin Structural-gray rule.
- Show period-start and period-end values side by side with a subtle vertical divider. Use Primary ink for the start and Emerald, Orange, or Red for the end according to target status.
- Beneath the values state the target, attainment or variance, evidence-backed drivers, and one compact directional callout.
- All comparisons must use the same metric definition, population, timezone, unit, and reporting window. Disclose methodology or cohort changes.
- For inverse metrics, explicitly show that lower is better. Distinguish absolute change, percent change, and percentage-point change. Use `pp` or `pts` for percentage points.
- Avoid causal language unless supported by an experiment or credible analysis. Use `associated with` or `management interpretation` when causality is uncertain.

## Page 4 — Achievements and value delivered

- Use a `3/9` or `4/8` split. The left Forest-green panel contains one editorial thesis, a short Emerald rule, and a concise synthesis of the quarter's delivered value.
- Use the optional serif only for the thesis. Keep the supporting synthesis in sans-serif.
- On the right, place three equal White achievement cards across the top. Each has an Emerald number, outcome-led title, scope, and evidence.
- Use one wide White business-impact card beneath the three achievements. It should connect delivery to a measured customer, commercial, operational, or risk effect.
- A Soft-mint Executive Perspective inset may summarize the management interpretation. Attribute a direct quotation; otherwise label it as a synthesis.
- Separate shipped capability, adopted behavior, and realized outcome. If value has not yet materialized, state the measurement plan and date rather than claiming success early.
- Do not list routine activity, effort, or output as a major achievement without the change it created.

## Page 5 — Gaps, causes, and corrective actions

- Use two equal White panels. Add a thin Red top rail to the left and an Emerald top rail to the right.
- The left panel contains no more than three material gaps. For each, show the quantified miss, the business consequence, and a real causal explanation.
- The right panel contains one mapped corrective action for each material cause. Number the actions and keep their order aligned with the causes.
- Every action needs a named owner, due date, capacity or dependency requirement, measurable exit criterion, and review cadence.
- Root cause must explain the mechanism, not restate the symptom. Separate planning assumptions, process design, capacity constraints, external dependencies, and decision latency.
- Use blame-free language focused on systems, choices, and observable behavior.
- A compact Emerald process-guardrail label may appear at the bottom only when the rule, owner, and effective date are confirmed.

## Page 6 — Next-quarter OKRs and cross-team commitments

- Use a balanced `6/6` split with two White panels.
- The left panel contains the draft OKR framework: two or three numbered Objectives, each followed by two to four Key Results.
- Objectives should state qualitative outcomes. Key Results should measure evidence, not tasks. Every KR needs baseline, target, unit, population, period, owner, data source, and committed-versus-stretch classification.
- The right panel contains a cross-department dependency ledger. Each row states the partner team, required contribution, accountable counterpart, deadline or gate, alignment status, and impact if missed.
- Use Soft mint behind confirmed alignment labels. Do not label an item aligned, committed, or approved without evidence from the counterpart and a confirmation date.
- Finish with one pale strategic-commitment inset using a Forest-green left rail. It should state the team's chosen trade-off, capacity focus, and measurable next review—not introduce a new unsupported forecast.
- Next-quarter KRs must respond directly to the prior quarter's gaps, strengths, and constraints. Avoid unrelated aspiration.

## OKR measurement discipline

- Establish targets, definitions, owners, scoring scales, and weights before the quarter closes. Disclose any retrospective change.
- Show the scoring basis for binary, continuous, threshold, and inverse KRs. Do not average unlike percentages without normalization.
- Decide and disclose whether overachievement is capped in the overall score. If uncapped results are useful, show them separately from plan attainment.
- Distinguish committed and stretch KRs. Their interpretation may differ, but the distinction must be made before scoring.
- Preserve both target and actual. Do not convert a missed KR into a revised target after the fact.
- Maintain a scorecard version, data-lock timestamp, reviewer, and approval state. Corrections should be traceable.
- If an objective contains qualitative evidence, use a published rubric and named approver rather than an arbitrary percentage.

## Evidence and content integrity

- Never copy any preview fact, including organizations, functions, quarters, people, products, account counts, financial values, technical metrics, root causes, actions, or commitments.
- Never invent attainment, revenue, usage, retention, conversion, latency, reliability, delivery, account growth, customer impact, cost, headcount, or partner alignment.
- State the reporting quarter, comparison period, data-lock time, timezone where material, currency, population, scope, and source.
- Define metric names, units, denominators, directionality, and exclusions. Keep those definitions stable between the scorecard and comparison pages.
- Reconcile the overall score to objective and KR scores. Reconcile achievement claims to the metric evidence. Reconcile corrective actions and next-quarter KRs to the diagnosed gaps.
- Distinguish actual, preliminary actual, estimate, forecast, target, stretch target, and management judgment.
- If evidence is incomplete, label the claim preliminary and state the validation owner and date. Use `TBD` only when an accountable follow-up exists.
- Preserve misses, nulls, and denominator changes. Never omit inconvenient evidence to improve the visual story.

## Adaptation

- The system can support product, engineering, sales, marketing, operations, finance, people, customer success, or cross-functional teams.
- Replace metrics and operational language while keeping target-versus-actual evidence, transparent scoring, traceable causes, accountable actions, and confirmed dependencies.
- Use one to three objectives on the main scorecard and place the complete KR register in an appendix when necessary.
- A non-quarterly team may use monthly, half-year, or program-cycle periods if the title, comparison window, and scoring controls are updated consistently.
- A final commitment slide may return to Cover charcoal, but ordinary evidence pages remain light.
- Localize language, date formats, and number formats while preserving the hierarchy and color semantics.

## Avoid

- Do not turn this into a generic dashboard, project plan, annual report, roadmap, or motivational retrospective.
- Do not use photography, illustration, gradients, 3D charts, glass effects, rounded SaaS-card styling, large icon sets, or decorative data visualization.
- Do not show an overall score without formula, weights, thresholds, cap rule, and missing-data treatment.
- Do not call output an outcome, activity an achievement, improvement a target hit, or an unconfirmed request a commitment.
- Do not claim causation from a simple before-and-after comparison.
- Do not show more than three objectives, four KRs per objective, three comparison metrics, three achievements, three root causes, or four dependencies on one main page.
- Do not mix cohorts, definitions, currencies, or reporting windows without disclosure.
- Do not shrink evidence, owners, dates, sources, formulas, or status definitions below readable size.
